# Before the first class {background-color="#E3120B" style="color:#F7F4ED"}

::: {style="margin-top: 1.0em; color:#F7F4ED"}
### Work through this at your desk. Budget 60–90 minutes.
:::

## What you are building

Six pieces, in this order. Each one checks before you move on.

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| **1** | VS Codium | the editor — Visual Studio Code without the telemetry |
| **2** | Extensions | Python support, from the Open VSX registry |
| **3** | The course materials | this repository, on your Desktop |
| **4** | Python | and a project environment, `.venv` |
| **5** | Ollama + Qwen 2.5 Coder | a language model that runs **on your machine** |
| **6** | aider | the agent you talk to in the terminal |

::: {.warn}
**Session 1 does not include installation time.** Arriving without a working environment means you
cannot take part in either half.
:::

## Where do I type this?

::: {.check}
**Always the VS Codium terminal.** Not the macOS Terminal, not PowerShell.
:::

Open it with **Terminal → New Terminal**, or ``Ctrl + ` ``.

::: {.step}
Why it matters: the VS Codium terminal starts inside your project folder and sees your `.venv`. The
system terminal does neither, which is the single most common reason a command that "should work"
does not.
:::

## Why local, and why these tools

::: {.tight}
- **VS Codium** — the same editor as VS Code, without telemetry, from a registry you can inspect
- **Ollama + Qwen** — the model runs on your laptop. No API key, no subscription, no data leaving
  the machine
- **aider** — an agent in the terminal, so you can see every command it proposes before it runs
:::

::: {.check}
Data sovereignty is a real constraint in the work you will do. A workflow that only functions when
you can send the data to somebody else's server is not a workflow you can take to a client.
:::

## Step 1 — VS Codium

Download from **[vscodium.com](https://vscodium.com)** and install it as you would any application.

::: {.step}
You will live in two panels: the **editor** on the right, and the **terminal** below it. Everything
in this course happens in one or the other.
:::

## Step 2 — Extensions

VS Codium uses the **Open VSX** registry, not Microsoft's Marketplace.

::: {.tight}
- **Python** (ms-python) — syntax, linting, the interpreter picker
- **Jupyter** — for running cells inside a file
- **Quarto** — to preview the lecture decks
:::

::: {.tight}
- **Continue** — the assistant panel inside the editor, which Step 5b points at
  your local model
:::

::: {.muted}
Extensions view: **View → Extensions**, or `Cmd/Ctrl + Shift + X`.
:::

## Step 3 — The course materials

Download the repository as a ZIP, unzip it **directly on your Desktop**, and keep the folder name:

```text
Desktop/quantitative-methods
```

Then **File → Open Folder** and choose it.

::: {.warn}
Every command in this course assumes you are in that folder. If your paths differ, nothing else on
these slides will work.
:::

::: {.muted}
In Session 02 you will do this properly, with git and your own group branch.
:::

## Step 4 — Python and the environment

The command is **not the same on the two platforms**. Use the one for yours.

**macOS and Linux**

```bash
python3 --version          # 3.11 or newer
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
```

**Windows** — `py`, the launcher that ships with Python. There is no `python3`
on Windows.

```powershell
py --version               # 3.11 or newer
py -m venv .venv
.venv\Scripts\activate
```

Then, on both:

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

::: {.check}
Your prompt should now begin with `(.venv)`. If it does not, the activation did
not take — and nothing installed afterwards will be visible to the course.
:::

## Windows: "Python introuvable"

If `py` or `python` prints **Python introuvable / Python was not found** and
offers you the Microsoft Store, do **not** accept. There are two causes and the
first is the common one.

::: {.step}
**1 · The Store alias is shadowing Python.** Windows ships a stub named
`python.exe` that does nothing but open the Store.

Start → search **Manage app execution aliases** → turn **off** both
**python.exe** and **python3.exe**. Close the terminal and open a new one.
:::

::: {.step}
**2 · Python is not installed, or not on PATH.** Install from
[python.org/downloads](https://www.python.org/downloads/) — not the Store — and
on the first screen tick **Add python.exe to PATH** before clicking Install.
That checkbox is off by default and is the single most common setup failure.
:::

## Windows: checking it took

Open a **new** terminal — PATH changes do not reach a terminal that is already
running.

```powershell
py --version
where py
```

::: {.check}
A version number and a path under `Program Files` or `AppData` means you are
fine. A path ending in `WindowsApps` means the Store alias is still in the way:
go back and turn it off.
:::

::: {.muted}
`py` is the right command on Windows even once PATH is set — it finds every
installed version and picks the newest. Inside an activated `.venv`, plain
`python` works and refers to the environment's own interpreter.
:::

## Step 5 — Ollama and Qwen

Install **[ollama.com](https://ollama.com)**, then in the VS Codium terminal:

```bash
ollama --version
ollama pull qwen2.5-coder
ollama pull nomic-embed-text
```

::: {.muted}
The second model is used in Session 09 for text embeddings. Pull it now while you have bandwidth.
:::

Check it answers:

```bash
ollama run qwen2.5-coder "In one sentence, what is a residual?"
```

::: {.check}
**Turn your wifi off and run that again.** It should still answer. That is the point of running it
locally.
:::

## Step 5b — Point Continue at your local model

Installed, Continue still talks to nothing. Give it a config at
`~/.continue/config.yaml` — on Windows, `%USERPROFILE%\\.continue\\config.yaml`:

```yaml
name: qmib
version: 0.0.1
models:
  - name: Local coder
    provider: ollama
    model: qwen2.5-coder:7b     # the size you actually pulled
    roles: [chat, edit, apply]
  - name: Local embedder
    provider: ollama
    model: nomic-embed-text
    roles: [embed]
context:
  - provider: file
  - provider: code
  - provider: diff
  - provider: terminal
```

::: {.check}
Open a `.py` file, select a few lines, press `Cmd/Ctrl + L`. If the panel
answers, you are done. If it answers nothing, `ollama serve` is not running.
:::

## Which model size

```bash
ollama pull qwen2.5-coder:3b     # 8 GB RAM
ollama pull qwen2.5-coder:7b     # 16 GB  ← most laptops
ollama pull qwen2.5-coder:14b    # 32 GB+
```

::: {.warn}
Pull the one that matches your **RAM**, not the biggest one. A model that does
not fit swaps to disk, and a 30-second answer becomes a five-minute one. Change
the name in `config.yaml` to whichever you pulled.
:::

## Step 6 — Give the model a real context window

Ollama defaults to a **2,048-token** context. aider fills that with your file and
the model then "forgets" what you sent. Raise it on the **server**, which is the
only place the setting is read.

**macOS** — the Ollama app is already serving, so setting the variable in a
terminal does nothing. Set it for the app, then restart it from the menu bar:

```bash
launchctl setenv OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH 8192
```

**Windows and Linux** — run the server yourself, in its own terminal:

```powershell
$env:OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH = "8192"; ollama serve
```

```bash
OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=8192 ollama serve       # Linux
```

::: {.warn}
`address already in use` means a server is **already running** — on macOS that
is the app, and you want `launchctl`, not this command.
:::

## Step 6b — The agent in your terminal

```bash
pip install aider-chat
```

Point it at the server. The variable goes in *aider's* terminal:

```bash
export OLLAMA_API_BASE=http://127.0.0.1:11434          # macOS / Linux
```

```powershell
$env:OLLAMA_API_BASE = "http://127.0.0.1:11434"        # Windows
```

Then, on both:

```bash
aider --model ollama_chat/qwen2.5-coder:7b
```

::: {.warn}
`ollama_chat/`, not `ollama/` — the second uses the completion endpoint and
gives markedly worse answers. And use the tag you actually pulled: `:3b`, `:7b`
or `:14b`.
:::

## Step 6c — Ask it something real

::: {.step}
*"Open `qmib.py` and explain what `load` does when the file is already cached."*
:::

Read what it proposes **before** you accept it. aider commits automatically
after each change it applies, and those commits are attributed to you.

```bash
aider --model ollama_chat/qwen2.5-coder:7b --no-auto-commits
```

::: {.muted}
`--no-auto-commits` if you would rather stage the changes yourself. Either way,
you are answerable for every line on your branch.
:::

## Two terminals is the working pattern

::: {.tight}
- **One** running `aider`, where you talk to the model
- **One** running `python`, where you check what it told you
:::

::: {.muted}
Plus the server — but on macOS that is the app in your menu bar, and on Windows
and Linux it is a terminal you start once and leave alone.
:::

::: {.warn}
The checking terminal is not optional. Every deliverable in this course requires
you to document one thing the model got wrong — and you cannot do that without
checking.
:::

## The last check

```bash
python 01-foundations-scenarios-and-tools/00-pre-session/verify_environment.py
```

::: {.check}
Five checks should pass. **Bring the output to class.**
:::

If one fails, the script prints what to do. If you are still stuck, ask Qwen — which is itself a
test of whether your setup works.

## When it goes wrong

| What you see | Why | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `Python introuvable` (Windows) | Store alias shadowing Python | Turn off the app execution aliases — two slides back |
| `ollama: command not found` | Not on PATH yet | New terminal; on Windows restart VS Codium |
| `ModuleNotFoundError` in VS Codium | Wrong interpreter selected | `Cmd/Ctrl + Shift + P` → *Python: Select Interpreter* → `.venv` |
| `pip` fails | Environment not active | Check your prompt starts with `(.venv)` |
| Continue answers nothing | `ollama serve` not running | Start it in its own terminal, leave it open |
| The model is very slow | Too large for your RAM | Pull `:3b` and change `config.yaml` |
| aider forgets your file | Ollama's 2k default context | Raise it on the **server** — step 6. macOS: `launchctl setenv`, not `ollama serve` |
| `connection refused` from aider | No server on 11434 | macOS: open the Ollama app. Windows/Linux: `ollama serve` |
| Maths shows as raw `$...$` | No preview extension | Install *Markdown Preview Enhanced*, open with `Cmd/Ctrl + K V` |
| Slow on Apple Silicon | Rosetta build of Python | Install the arm64 build |

## Using the model well

The local model is a **sparring partner**, not an oracle.

::: {.step}
**Ask it to argue against you.** Its most useful output is the objection you had
not considered — not the answer you were hoping for.
:::

::: {.step}
**Verify every factual claim.** It states plausible falsehoods with complete
confidence, and does so most often about library APIs, statistical results and
citations — which is exactly the material of this course.
:::

::: {.step}
**Record what you checked.** Every practice deliverable requires one documented
instance where you caught the model being wrong or unable to support a claim.
That is graded.
:::

::: {.warn}
You are never penalised for using the model. You are penalised for using it
uncritically.
:::
